title: Reverse a doubly linked list
summary: Swap next and prev in every node, then move head to the old last node.

checkpoints.text: Node 1 has swapped its arrows: `next` is now NULL, because it will be the last node, and `prev` points at 2. To move on, the loop follows `prev`, because the swap just put the old `next` there.
Node 2 swapped too: its `next` points at 1 and its `prev` at 3.
`temp` holds the last swapped `prev`, which was node 2. Its `prev` is now node 3, the new first node, so `head` moves there.
3 2 1. Every node was visited once, so reversing is O(n), and no node was created or deleted.
